correctness.rationale: For composite n and T(n)=product_{d|n} d=n^(τ(n)/2), expansion of V(n)/2=product_{d>1}(d+1) gives V/2≥σ+T, equality exactly when τ=3 (prime square). For τ=3, n=p², 7T-8σ=(p-2)(7p²+6p+4)≥0 equality only p=2. If τ=4, n≥6, T=n² and σ≤4n give T/σ≥n/4≥3/2. If τ≥5, n≥12, T/σ≥n^(τ/2-1)/τ≥12^(3/2)/5>8/7, because the t-bound increases for t≥5. Thus V≥(30/7)σ and equality exactly n=4. Independently checked all 8,770 composite integers through 10,000 exactly, but infinitude comes from the symbolic divisor-count split.
